claims.claim: All elements heavier than H/He (trace Li) are forged in stars
claims.citation: B²FH: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle, Rev. Mod. Phys. 29, 547 (1957); Fowler Nobel Prize in Physics 1983

claims.claim: Binding energy per nucleon peaks near Fe-56/Ni-62; iron fusion absorbs energy, causing core collapse in massive stars
claims.citation: Measured nuclear binding energy curve; core-collapse supernova theory

claims.claim: Supernova ejecta iron is born as Ni-56 → Co-56 → Fe-56; confirmed by SN 1987A light curve (~77 d Co-56 half-life) and gamma-ray lines
Core-collapse remnants are neutron stars (~20 km); the Crab pulsar is the remnant of SN 1054
An adult human body contains ~3-4 g of iron, mostly in hemoglobin; solar-system iron isotopes match stellar yields
